greeting.text: Well met. The forge is hot if you need steel.

warn.text: Bandits camp east of the mill. Kestrel keeps them off us — buys his blades from me, so I've a stake in him coming home.

kin.text: Elowen the trader's my sister. She keeps the coin, I keep the coal. We do well enough between us.

grieve_elowen.text: My sister. The shop's shuttered and the forge feels twice as cold. Whoever did it had best pray the guard finds them before I do.

mourn.text: We've buried one of our own lately. If you've a strong arm, the road east could use watching.

inventory.name: Bread
inventory.description: A heel of bread. Restores a little health.

greeting.text: Coin for potions, potions for coin. What'll it be?

responses.text: Where do your goods come from?

supply.text: Bram's farm keeps my shelves stocked — bread, flax, what have you. My brother Thalen forges the rest into something worth selling.

grieve_thalen.text: My brother, gone. He was all bluster and hammer, but he was mine. Don't expect me to smile today.

inventory.name: Bread
inventory.description: A heel of bread. Restores a little health.

greeting.text: Long day in the fields. The crop's good this year, thank the gods.

mara.text: Mara? Down at the square, most days. She fancies the guard, Kestrel — thinks I don't notice. Good lad, though. I'll allow it.

grieve_mara.text: My little sister. I keep looking up expecting her to come down the lane. The fields can rot for all I care today.

greeting.text: Move along, citizen. I've bandits to watch for.

responses.text: Anyone you're watching over in particular?

mara.text: The whole town. But... Mara, if you're asking. Don't you dare let anything happen to her while I'm out on the wall.

grieve_mara.text: Say her name again and I'll not answer for what I do. I'll cut down every last bandit east of the mill, or die trying.

greeting.text: Spare a coin? A man's got to eat...

gossip.text: Me? I hear everything. Owe old Thalen three silver, mind — don't tell him you saw me. And that guard's sweet on Mara, if you didn't know.

gossip_mourn.text: Aye. A death in a place this small, everyone feels it. Even a beggar bows his head. Coin doesn't warm you the same after.

greeting.text: Millbrook's a quiet place, mostly. We like it that way.

responses.text: Kestrel fell defending the town. I'm sorry.

folk.text: My brother Bram works the east fields. And Kestrel keeps the square — he pretends it's duty, but he lingers by me longer than the others.

grieve_kestrel.text: He said he'd always come home from the wall. He lied. I don't know how to be here without him watching the square.

grieve_bram.text: My brother. The farm's just dirt now, without him cursing at the crows. I've no one left but the memory of him.
